texts.facts: The present petition has been filed assailing the order dated 09.06.2025 passed by the respondent No.3 whereby a new Expression of Interest No.4054 has been issued deleting the conditions mentioned in the earlier Expression of Interest just to extend the benefit to private respondent Nos.4 to 8. 2. It is the case of the petitioner that he is registered as a road milk transporter duly registered with Government of Madhya Pradesh, Food and Drugs Administration Food Safety and Standards Authority of India having registration certificate no.21423730001793. The respondent no.2/Bhopal Sahkari Dugdh Sangh Maryadit is affiliated to M.P. State Cooperative Dairy NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:69989 2 WP-22961-2025 Federation, Bhopal and is in existence since 1977. It covers 11 districts and deals with 22 milk chilling centres in its area of operation. The main dairy plant of Bhopal Sahkari Dugdh Sangh is having 4.00 Lakhs litre per day capacity and is located at Habibganj Bhopal. The dairy development activities in the rural areas include conduct of survey of villages having milk potential, organizing primary milk cooperative society under M.P. Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, enrolling milk producers as its members, including cattle, collecting milk from Goravraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76723771/ 1 them, imparting training, supporting technical input service and extending the benefit under the various State and Central Government Schemes which goes to show that Bhopal Dugdh Sangh falls under the ambit of Article 12 of the Constitution of India and is amenable to the writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. 3. The petitioner and respondent Nos.4 to 8 are involved in business of milk transportation. On 14-11-2024, the respondent no. 2, i.e., Bhopal Sahkari Dugdh Sangh Maryadit circulated Expression of Interest no.7849 for work of liquid milk transportation through milk tankers. Online applications were invited for attaching insulated milk tankers from various BMC routes located under the jurisdiction of Bhopal Milk Plant and Milk Cold Centre Narsinghgarh, Pachor, Shujalpur and Ashta. There were 37 essential conditions for application for milk tanker transporters. The petitioner as well as the respondent Nos.4 to 8 submitted their online application for obtaining the tender. The petitioner fulfilled all the required qualifications and he has attached all the relevant documents along with his application. The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:69989 3 WP-22961-2025 respondent Nos.4 to 8 were not fulfilling all the conditions. They were aggrieved by condition nos.10 and 32. Therefore, there was very possibility that their tender application may be cancelled. 4. The respondent nos.4 to 8 preferred a writ petition being W.P.No.38143 of 2024 before this Court challenging the validity of clause 1 and its sub-clause of Form no.1 read with clause 11 of Form no. 2 and Clause 10 and clause 32 of Form no.2 of NIT dated 14-11-2024. When the matter was listed for consideration, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 & 3 has submitted that they have been instructed to withdraw the tender under challenge and want to float a new tender. Therefore, said writ petition was disposed off vide order 13.05.2025 granting liberty to them to float a new tender. The petitioner and the respondents were granted liberty to participate in new tender proceedings. In view of the same, the respondent Nos.2 & 3 on 09.06.2025 issued a fresh Expression of Interest No.4953 for the same purpose. Last date for submission of applications was 30.06.2025 at 12:00 noon. with a condition of attaching EMD amounting to Rs.1,00,000/-. It is the case of the petitioner that the respondents have deleted condition nos.10, 11, 29, 32, 33 and 34 of the earlier expression of interest no.7849 dated 14-11-2024 from the new Expression of Interest No.4953 dated 09.06.2025 and the same has been done just to extend the benefit to respondent nos.4 to 8. On notice being issued, a detailed reply has been filed by the respondent Nos.2 & 3. They have denied the petition's averments.
texts.arguments: It is pointed out that there were 37 essential conditions in the earlier expression of interest which are now being reduced by deleting 6 essential conditions which are going against the interest of the Bhopal Sahkari Dugdh Sangh Maryadit and the same has been done in connivance NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:69989 4 WP-22961-2025 with the respondent nos.4 to 8 just to extend them undue advantage. It is argued that the cancellation of the earlier tender was totally unwarranted as the required condition are the essential conditions mentioned in the NIT were in the interest of the respondent Nos.2 & 3. No reasons have been assigned by the authorities for withdrawal of the earlier tender or Expression of Interest which was floated. Learned counsel for the petitioner has pointed out that the reasons are required to be assigned for withdrawing the tender proceedings initiated earlier. They cannot be substituted by any other reasons which are not a part of the decision taken by the authorities placing upon a judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the Mohinder Singh Gill and another vs. The Chief Election Commissioner, New Delhi and others reported in 1978 (1) SCC 405. Therefore, this petition has been filed. Goravraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76723771/ 2 5. A preliminary objection is raised that this petition is not maintainable as the petitioner is having no locus to file this petition. It is contended that there is no document placed on record to show that the petitioner is a participant in the tender proceedings. Once the petitioner is not a participant to the tender proceedings, how he can be said to be an aggrieved person. Second objection is taken with respect to maintainability of the writ petition on the ground that the interested parties are not made party to the proceedings. They have not impleaded the CEO or the respondent/organization in the array of respondents who has issued the Expression of Interest. Without impleading the CEO a party to the proceedings, the petition is not maintainable. It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:69989 5 WP-22961-2025 further contended that the authorities were well within their jurisdiction to recall the earlier tender proceedings and to call for a new tender proceedings. The same cannot be subject matter of judicial review. Earlier tender proceedings were not finalized and no right or interest was created in favour of the petitioner. In W.P.No.38143 of 2024 vide interim order dated 02.12.2024 finalization of previous tender proceedings was stayed. Therefore, the authorities have withdrawn the previous tender proceedings and said writ petition was disposed off granting liberty to them to float a new Expression of Interest. In view of the [LEAKAGE_MASK], they have floated a new Expression of Interest. The petitioner as well as the private respondents were granted liberty to participate in the said proceedings. The petitioner himself has chosen not to participate in the fresh proceedings. Therefore, no relief can be extended to the petitioner. 6. A separate reply has been filed by the respondent Nos.4 to 8 raising the similar objections regarding locus of the petitioner and maintainability of the writ petition. The said aspect was highlighted by the respondents by filing an application being I.A.No.3285 of 2025 for taking subsequent facts on record in W.P.No.38143 of 2024. The petitioner was a beneficiary of the said stopgap arrangement and his tankers are deployed even now for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:69989 6 WP-22961-2025 transportation of milk. Floating of a NIT, finalization of NIT is within the domain of the respondents. 7.
